correctness.rationale: For all b>=3 and k>=2, every circular zero gap is indexed by a 2-adic valuation or is the unique zero closing gap. Cyclic lex sorting partitions by remaining zero length. At each distinguished h_j, identical first 2^j-1 successor gaps and a strict three-way comparison at the 2^j-th successor give predecessor letters 1^(2^t-1)0^(2^t-1)1. All other zero-start rows carry zero; the one-start rows carry exactly one one, with zero endpoints for k>=2. These blocks imply 2k one-runs and 2k zero-runs; the original word has 2^(k+1)-1 runs. Bounded independent-generator and cyclic-rotation checks passed for 44 parameter cases; these do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The whole family of generalized Cantor words at all bases b>=3 and all levels k>=2 has a natural BWT run complexity. Exact 4k and the full ordered one-run spectrum (independent of b) refine existing asymptotic bounds by a structurally meaningful constant and cluster-shape invariant. The result gives a sharp run-length storage measure and exact clustering ratio 4k/(2^(k+1)-1), using a nontrivial valuation-based lexicographic argument rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
